_README: What each principle on the rail is called in the literature, and where it is stated. This file also DECIDES what the page is willing to call a principle: a rail root with no entry here is refused by `dag.py --conform`, and a statement of this development's own -- max attainment over a compact space, say -- has no entry and so never reaches the rail. A principle listed here that no published landmark reaches is named in the panel rather than drawn, so the rail stays a picture of what the published tree pays for.

EM.name: the law of excluded middle
cite: Troelstra and van Dalen, Constructivism in Mathematics: An Introduction, North-Holland (1988).
Diener, Constructive Reverse Mathematics, arXiv:1804.05495 (2020).

WEM.name: the weak law of excluded middle
WEM.note: Equivalent over intuitionistic logic to the third De Morgan law, that a negated conjunction splits into a disjunction of negations.
cite: Diener, Constructive Reverse Mathematics, arXiv:1804.05495 (2020).
Ishihara, Reverse mathematics in Bishop's constructive mathematics, Philosophia Scientiae CS 6 (2006), 43-59.

LPO.name: the limited principle of omniscience
cite: Bishop, Foundations of Constructive Analysis, McGraw-Hill (1967).
Bridges and Richman, Varieties of Constructive Mathematics, London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series 97, Cambridge University Press (1987).
Diener, Constructive Reverse Mathematics, arXiv:1804.05495 (2020).

WLPO.name: the weak limited principle of omniscience
cite: Bridges and Richman, Varieties of Constructive Mathematics, London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series 97, Cambridge University Press (1987).
Diener, Constructive Reverse Mathematics, arXiv:1804.05495 (2020).

LLPO.name: the lesser limited principle of omniscience
cite: Bishop, Foundations of Constructive Analysis, McGraw-Hill (1967).
Bridges and Richman, Varieties of Constructive Mathematics, London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series 97, Cambridge University Press (1987).
Diener, Constructive Reverse Mathematics, arXiv:1804.05495 (2020).

SignDisjunction.name: the lesser limited principle of omniscience, in its analytic form
SignDisjunction.note: That every real is non-positive or non-negative. This is the form LLPO takes over the reals rather than a separate principle.
cite: Bridges and Richman, Varieties of Constructive Mathematics, London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series 97, Cambridge University Press (1987).
Diener, Constructive Reverse Mathematics, arXiv:1804.05495 (2020).

MP.name: Markov's principle
cite: Troelstra and van Dalen, Constructivism in Mathematics: An Introduction, North-Holland (1988).
Bridges and Richman, Varieties of Constructive Mathematics, London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series 97, Cambridge University Press (1987).
Diener, Constructive Reverse Mathematics, arXiv:1804.05495 (2020).

FANΔ.name: the decidable fan theorem
also: the fan theorem for detachable bars
cite: Troelstra and van Dalen, Constructivism in Mathematics: An Introduction, North-Holland (1988).
Ishihara, Constructive reverse mathematics: compactness properties, in From Sets and Types to Topology and Analysis, Oxford Logic Guides 48, Oxford University Press (2005), 245-267.

FANstable.name: the fan theorem for stable bars
cite: Ishihara, Constructive reverse mathematics: compactness properties, in From Sets and Types to Topology and Analysis, Oxford Logic Guides 48, Oxford University Press (2005), 245-267.

WKL.name: weak Koenig's lemma
WKL.note: The base system WKL_0 of classical reverse mathematics is named for it. Over a constructive base it is the contrapositive companion of the fan theorem rather than a consequence of it.
cite: Simpson, Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic, second edition, Cambridge University Press (2009).
Ishihara, Constructive reverse mathematics: compactness properties, in From Sets and Types to Topology and Analysis, Oxford Logic Guides 48, Oxford University Press (2005), 245-267.

WKLBool.name: weak Koenig's lemma, with the tree given by a decision procedure
WKLBool.note: Weak Koenig's lemma with membership presented as a Boolean-valued function rather than as a disjunction in Prop. The split is this development's, and it isolates the carrier upgrade the Prop form performs; the base system WKL_0 of classical reverse mathematics is named for the lemma itself.
cite: Simpson, Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic, second edition, Cambridge University Press (2009).
Ishihara, Constructive reverse mathematics: compactness properties, in From Sets and Types to Topology and Analysis, Oxford Logic Guides 48, Oxford University Press (2005), 245-267.

DC.name: the axiom of dependent choice
cite: Jech, The Axiom of Choice, North-Holland (1973).
Howard and Rubin, Consequences of the Axiom of Choice, Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 59, American Mathematical Society (1998).

DCOn.name: the axiom of dependent choice, on a single set
DCOn.note: Dependent choice with the set fixed rather than quantified. The restriction is this development's: every consumer here spends the hypothesis on a set it has already built, so the quantifier is never used.
cite: Jech, The Axiom of Choice, North-Holland (1973).
Howard and Rubin, Consequences of the Axiom of Choice, Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 59, American Mathematical Society (1998).

TreeDC.name: dependent choice along a binary tree
TreeDC.note: That a predicate on finite binary strings which always extends by one bit admits an infinite string through it. A form of dependent choice specialised to the binary tree; the spelling is this development's.
cite: Jech, The Axiom of Choice, North-Holland (1973).
Diener, Constructive Reverse Mathematics, arXiv:1804.05495 (2020).

BinaryDC.name: countable choice from two-element sets
BinaryDC.note: Proved here to be equivalent to countable Boolean choice: its whole content is turning a disjunction in Prop into a Bool along a recursion, which makes it a choice principle rather than an omniscience one.
cite: Howard and Rubin, Consequences of the Axiom of Choice, Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 59, American Mathematical Society (1998).
Herrlich, Axiom of Choice, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1876, Springer (2006).

BinaryDCOn.name: countable choice from two-element sets, on a single set
BinaryDCOn.note: The binary choice principle with the carrier fixed rather than quantified, for the same reason `DCOn` fixes it.
cite: Howard and Rubin, Consequences of the Axiom of Choice, Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 59, American Mathematical Society (1998).

ACOmega.name: the axiom of countable choice
cite: Jech, The Axiom of Choice, North-Holland (1973).
Herrlich, Axiom of Choice, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1876, Springer (2006).

MonotoneConvergence.name: the monotone convergence theorem
MonotoneConvergence.note: Classically a theorem, taken as a hypothesis here because its constructive strength is what is being measured.
cite: Bridges and Richman, Varieties of Constructive Mathematics, London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series 97, Cambridge University Press (1987).
Diener, Constructive Reverse Mathematics, arXiv:1804.05495 (2020).
